title: Why? #4: why sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 (unit circle + stacked bar) → NDA 2025 (I) Q35 (48 s, bright music)

captions.instagram:
Why? #4 · Why is sin²θ + cos²θ always 1? ⭕

Put a point on a circle of radius 1. Its height is sin θ, its width is cos θ, and Pythagoras on that triangle gives sin²θ + cos²θ = 1.
Now spin the point: sin²θ and cos²θ trade places, one grows while the other shrinks, and the total never changes.

NDA 2025 (I) asked it (Maths Q35): p = sin α − sin(α − 90°). Maximum value of p?
sin(α − 90°) = −cos α, so p = sin α + cos α. They can't both be 1, so the best is when they're equal: 1/√2 + 1/√2 = √2 → (b).
Trap: (d) 2 needs sin and cos to be 1 at the same time.
